def min_equal_pair_flips(s: str, t: str) -> int:
    """
    Minimum flips of cyclically adjacent equal pairs to turn necklace s into t.

    s and t are strings over '0'/'1' of the same even length n, 4 <= n <= 200.
    They describe values at n fixed positions on a circle: position i is
    adjacent to position (i+1) % n, so position n-1 is adjacent to position 0.

    One operation: choose two cyclically adjacent positions that currently
    hold EQUAL characters and flip both of them (the pair "00" becomes "11",
    or "11" becomes "00"; a pair "01" or "10" may never be chosen).

    Return the minimum number of operations that transforms s into t, as an
    int, or -1 if no sequence of operations does. Note the state space has
    2**n states, so brute-force search is hopeless at n = 200.

    >>> min_equal_pair_flips("0000", "1111")
    2
    >>> min_equal_pair_flips("0000", "0111")
    -1
    >>> min_equal_pair_flips("10010101", "01011001")
    6
    """
